title: Decode worker construction
summary: Recover 0x48d6e0 as a genuine thiscall member initializer with explicit partial layout, original import bindings, event creation, thread launch and priority mapping. Preserve unchecked event failures and the thread-handle comparison against -1. Original caller 0x44e680 constructs a +0x130 member; entry token 0x48dc50 invokes vtable slot +8. Accepted reference independently matches all 234 bytes of Game.exe.
test_description: GCC i386 freestanding differential harness passed 288 paired cases: three initial byte patterns, four thread handles including zero and -1, six callback-written priority modes, successful/failed event returns, and written/untouched thread ID. Both routines are checked against identical expected complete byte images at every import and after return, including guards and untouched fields. Verify exact event and begin-thread arguments, callback order, thread-entry token, return-this identity, ignored priority-call failure, priority bypass only for -1, and normal-path FS head restoration after every call. Exactly 4096 bytes of oracle_iat linked at 0x92d000; oracle text linked at 0x48d6e0. Locally assembled reference compared directly against original PE bytes.
known_limits: High-level unmatched recovery; no matching-source credit claimed.
Fixed original IAT, vtable and thread-entry address tokens require platform integration for a Linux port. Controlled callbacks do not implement Windows events, CRT thread creation or scheduling.
Only the constructor is recovered. Thread entry and decoding are not executed. Concurrent thread behavior, exceptional callbacks and Windows exception unwinding are untested.
The layout is partial through offset 0x14c; complete object size and meaning of request/output words remain unresolved. Trailing C++ alignment padding has no recovered semantics.
Pinned native Windows compilation is left to trusted validation; optional local MSVC helper is unavailable.
